comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C28-C33 regarding Experiment 1 behavioral findings. Both evaluations find the evidence for sensory preconditioned fear with 8 and 32 pairings to be well-supported, with appropriate statistical evidence and controls. OpenEval emphasizes statistical details (F-tests, p<0.001, effect sizes) while peer reviewers provide explicit affirmations from all three reviewers.

Strong agreement on claims C36-C40 regarding pharmacological findings from Experiments 2A/2B. Both evaluations support the differential effect of DAP5 on sensory preconditioned fear. Peer review additionally includes C56 (a summary claim) and emphasizes the consistency with prior work, while OpenEval focuses on the logical inference about distinct integration mechanisms.

Strong agreement on claims C43-C48 regarding disconnection experiments 3A/3B. Both evaluations support the finding that PRh-BLA disconnection during stage 2 selectively impairs sensory preconditioned fear after 8 but not 32 pairings. Peer review additionally includes C57 (summary claim) and emphasizes consistency with Wong et al. 2019, while OpenEval highlights the anatomical logic and control design.

Strong agreement on claims C49-C54 regarding disconnection experiments 4A/4B. Both evaluations support the opposite pattern (disconnection at test affects 32-pairing but not 8-pairing condition). Peer review additionally includes C58 (summary claim) and emphasizes this as a key novel contribution, while OpenEval highlights the double dissociation logic providing converging evidence.

Agreement on primary conclusions C3-C5, C55. Both evaluations support the overarching finding of distinct integration mechanisms. OpenEval includes additional summary claims (C56-C58) and emphasizes the converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers emphasize the clarity, consistency, and high impact of the findings, calling the study 'highly impactful and significant.'

Agreement on background claims C1, C15-C20 from prior work (Wong et al. 2019). Both evaluations accept these as appropriately cited foundational claims. OpenEval includes C21 and emphasizes how current study extends these findings, while peer reviewers note this as an important follow-up to prior work. Peer review includes C2 which OpenEval does not address in this result.

Divergent evaluations on mechanistic hypothesis claims C22-C24, C59-C60. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis is plausible but speculative since order learning is not directly tested. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating the interpretation as reasonable and well-grounded in cited literature. Peer reviewers note the discussion offers 'insightful interpretations' without challenging the speculation.

Divergent evaluations on mechanistic claims C61-C64. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting directionality claims are speculative and not directly tested (would require pathway-specific manipulations). Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating these as valuable contributions and 'plausible and testable' hypotheses. Peer review also includes C68-C71 which OpenEval addresses separately in R8.

Divergent evaluations on speculative mechanism claims C65-C71 (PRh-CeA pathway hypothesis). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing these are 'entirely speculative and not tested' and represent future directions rather than supported findings. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, praising the hypothesis as 'excellent' and 'very much worth exploring,' treating speculation as a strength rather than limitation.

Agreement on methodological claims C74-C89 regarding surgical procedures, drug preparation, and histological verification. Both evaluations find these well-documented and appropriate. OpenEval emphasizes sufficient detail for replication and transparent exclusion reporting. Peer review combines these with behavioral methods (C90-C97) in a single evaluation praising overall methodological rigor.

Agreement on behavioral methods claims C90-C97. Both evaluations support these as appropriate, with OpenEval specifically praising blind observers, inter-rater reliability verification, and a priori power analysis. Peer reviewers combine these with surgical methods in a single evaluation emphasizing 'careful, rigorous experimental design and statistics' and 'high quality of writing.'

OpenEval evaluates claims C25-C27, C34-C35, C41-C42 regarding prior literature on PRh-BLA communication and NMDA receptor manipulations as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background/rationale claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C72-C73 acknowledging other brain regions involved in sensory preconditioning as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate contextualization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately address these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates background claims C6-C14 (established knowledge about memory, standard protocols, illustrative examples) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these introductory/background claims.
